title: African rice gall midge on rice - Sierra Leone

Header: African rice gall midge on rice - Sierra Leone

Prevention: Use tolerant rice varieties, such as ‘Rok 24’ Clear wild grasses from around the nursery site
Brush and burn weeds found around the field
Brush and burn or remove weeds and rice stubble during off- planting season
Monitoring: During nursery stage and after transplanting into field, look for symptoms of gall midge attack
Symptoms include the appearance of onion leaf (yabbas leaf) or the affected tillers becoming white in colour
Direct Control: Uproot individual affected tillers and bury or burn
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Apply in the evening or morning when adult midges are active.
Apply once per growing season before the flowering stage.
